Well, I haven't seen this Citigroup analysis, but fixed costs is not how you determine the cost of delivering a package. You have to look at the full cost - fixed + variable. So, the cost to lease a warehouse, the cost to lease the local post office, the cost to purchase a mail vehicle, the cost of the fuel, the salary of the clerks, sorters, and carriers, etc. Add all that shit up, divide it by the number of pieces of mail delivered, and you have your cost per package. The USPS does this every year, they call it "Mail count." Every route is counted 1x every 3 years, guaranteed. Some routes in fast growing areas get counted 2-3 times a year.
